Elevated sintering temperature increases the relative density of the fabricated composites from 97.2% (653 K) to 99.4% (853 K).
The elevated sintering temperature facilitates elemental exchange at the interfaces, where Cu diffuses into TiZrNbTa phase and preferentially dissolves in the Ti (Zr)-rich phase.

The enhanced strength may result from the reduction of internal defects due to improved densification during sintering, as well as the intensified interfacial bonding facilitated by interfacial diffusion.

the augmented interfacial elemental diffusion allows impurity atoms into the Cu matrix, leading to excessive electron scattering of the Cu matrix, which poses a greater negative impact on electrical conductivity than the positive impact of optimized interfacial bonding.

Compared to specimens obtained at a sintering temperature of 653 K, the yield strength of the specimens sintered at 813 K is increased by more than 200 MPa, while only 8% IACS reduction in electrical conductivity is achieved.
